identity.title: An Improved Clique-Picking Algorithm for Counting Markov Equivalent DAGs via Super Cliques Transfer

problem.claim: Efficiently count Markov equivalent DAGs from a given CPDAG.

gap.claim: The work targets more efficient generation of unresolved undirected connected components within the existing Clique-Picking procedure.

contributions.claim: A UCCG-generation approach that reuses results computed for different root cliques.
Super cliques within rooted clique trees, transferable between trees with different root cliques.

stated_novelty.claim: Introducing super cliques to enable efficient transfer across differently rooted clique trees.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the proposed algorithm reduces the computational complexity of Clique-Picking, especially when the number of cliques is substantially smaller than the number of vertices and edges.

narrative_sequence.summary: Counting Markov equivalent DAGs is presented as important for graphical causal analysis.
The prior polynomial-time Clique-Picking algorithm counts DAGs from a CPDAG by iteratively selecting root cliques, fixing orientations, and generating unresolved components.
The paper reuses computations across root cliques and introduces transferable super cliques in rooted clique trees.
The authors report reduced computational complexity under a specified relative-size condition on cliques, vertices, and edges.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links reuse of results across root choices with a complexity reduction, while identifying the regime where the reduction is particularly relevant.

lessons.interpretation: A method contribution can be made more informative by connecting an optimization mechanism to the structural regime in which it is expected to matter.
lessons.application: When proposing an algorithmic optimization, state both the reused intermediate structure and the input-size condition associated with the reported benefit.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the optimization has uniform guarantees or when no meaningful input regime distinguishes its impact.

unknowns: No quantitative runtime, complexity bound, dataset, baseline measurement, or proof details are supplied.
The abstract does not specify the exact super-clique transfer procedure or the meaning of “effectively” reducing complexity.
